sources.facts: Cunningham, 1862–63 field survey, sections 128–135. The south fort wall rises about 12.2 m above the scarp with remains of battlements. Quarry stone, battered wall faces, irregular circular bastions and domestic vault ruins. The red-and-white tomb is about 18.75 m square outside and 21.3 m to the dome, enclosed by a polygonal stone wall and approached along a masonry causeway.
ASI entries 138–139 describe the fort’s palace area west of the steps, the citadel to the east, surviving gates, rubble walls and bastions.
ASI 2002–03 field report records mostly below-ground palace fabric and excavated low stone walls west of the depression opposite the tomb causeway.
ASI yearly conservation report distinguishes the fort walls, the fortified tomb and separate Adilabad, and records reconstruction of southern bastions and wall repairs.
